reason: The industrial servo motor is currently a decomposition frontier, not a terminal node. Add stator, rotor, magnets, windings, encoder, housing, bearings, thermal design, motor-control interface, manufacturing processes, cost/supply constraints, and evidence.

title: Review whole robot agent-assisted decomposition import
reason: The whole parcel-sorting robot has now been expanded across vision, end effector, reducer, servo drive, conveyor integration, and decision/control branches. The imported claims are unreviewed and need human review before being treated as settled product knowledge.

title: Add parcel end-effector reliability evidence
reason: The suction/gripper branch is structurally decomposed, but pickup success, leakage, surface compatibility, blow-off timing, wear parts, and maintenance cost still need field or benchmark evidence.

title: Add field benchmark evidence for parcel vision
reason: The vision branch now has camera, optics, lighting, compute, and barcode/OCR software, but no-read rate, glare/occlusion robustness, latency, and parcel mix performance remain weakly evidenced.

title: Add conveyor integration and jam-rate evidence
reason: The conveyor branch now includes sensors, speed tracking, spacing, PLC/WCS integration, chutes, and jam recovery, but installed cost, commissioning time, jam modes, and operator recovery time still need field evidence.

title: Add reducer life, machining, and cost evidence
reason: The reducer branch now separates wave generator, flexspline, circular spline, output bearing, and life testing, but precision machining, fatigue, lubrication interval, backlash growth, and cost evidence remain incomplete.

title: Add raw-material quantity and supplier model for the robot BOM
reason: The robot graph now reaches copper, steel, aluminum, silicon, rare-earth, and elastomer feedstock chains, but it still lacks per-system quantities, supplier choices, price sensitivity, import dependence, and recycling assumptions.

title: Deepen rare-earth magnet supply chain evidence
reason: The magnet branch now reaches NdPr and heavy rare-earth feedstocks, but it needs evidence for separation/refining, metal/alloy conversion, magnet sintering, coating, recycling, substitution, and price volatility.

reason: Six roadmap test products were added with recursive product-to-material/process decomposition. The claims are intentionally unreviewed and need human review before promotion.

reason: The iPhone 4 graph reaches glass, semiconductor, battery, steel, and final assembly branches, but needs reviewed evidence for actual BOM suppliers, material mass, display/touch stack process, RF/enclosure issue history, and high-volume assembly yield.

title: Add fusion tritium, materials, and availability evidence
